entry.title: Home 1.0.0
entry.content:
# Home 1.0.0
Home is a plain, quiet home screen for E Ink phones, made on the Mudita Kompakt. It is [inkOS](https://github.com/gezimos/inkos) by gezimos, as its own app beside inkOS, with what the apps made to work with it need. Everything inkOS does still works, and a backup from inkOS restores into Home.
- **One Nextcloud account for the whole phone.** Sign in once, in the first run or in Settings → Nextcloud account. The apps that sign in to Nextcloud get a row "Use the phone's Nextcloud account": one tap there, and nothing to type. The password is locked on the phone and handed only to those apps, checked by their signing key. Signing out in Home signs them out too and deletes the password on the server. - **Your apps.** Settings → Your apps lists the apps made to work with Home, in folders (Core first), each one installed or missing, with Install and Update. A download is installed only if its size, checksum, package, version and signing key are the right ones. With no connection it shows the list Home carries, without installing. - **Settings in groups**: Phone, Apps, Home screen, Setup and about, in the same plain look as the other apps. inkOS's own pages and rows are all still there. - **Dark mode for all the apps.** On MuditaOS, Settings → Dark mode turns Home dark, and the other apps follow it. On other phones, Home follows the phone's own dark setting. - **A first run of its own**: welcome and privacy, setup, your apps, default apps, Nextcloud, theme and home apps. Settings → Run setup again opens it again; nothing is reset. - **Default apps.** One row for each kind of thing the apps open: calls, texts, contacts, calendar, alarms, gallery, maps, text files, passwords and more. Each row says what Android does today. - **Lines on home.** Up to three lines under the home apps from [Glance](https://github.com/wanderwildwood/hitome) 0.1.24 or later: today's events, the weather, what is unread. A press opens the app the line came from; a long press shows each source and what it is doing. The lines can sit at the top or at the bottom. - Also: music on the lock screen for any player, folders in the app drawer, E-ink mode per app on MuditaOS 2.0 and later, a contact found in search opens in Connections, all-day events show on their own date, and service notifications no longer badge their apps.
Unlike inkOS, Home has the internet permission, used only for Your apps and for your own Nextcloud server. Home has no server of its own and sends nothing about you.
1.0.0 installs over a 0.1.0 test build and keeps its settings.
Nearly all of Home is inkOS, by [gezimos](https://github.com/gezimos), under the GPL-3.0. Thank you. For plain inkOS, go to [gezimos's repository](https://github.com/gezimos/inkos).

entry.title: Memo 0.3.35
entry.content:
# Memo 0.3.35
- Nextcloud: a new row, "Use the phone's Nextcloud account", uses the account Home already holds, so there is nothing to sign in to here; the screen then says who, on which server, from Home, with "Stop using it" - When Home signs out of Nextcloud, Memo does too, and your notes and tasks stay on the phone; when Home has the same account again, Memo carries on with it - Your notes on the phone belong to one account: they are never sent to another one, and that account's own notes come back if it had some - Signing in by email works with an app password, and the Nextcloud user id is used for the notes folder and the task lists - Locked notes: hold a note and press Lock, with a PIN of 4 to 8 digits. A locked note is encrypted on the phone and stays there only: it leaves Nextcloud, Desktop Sync and Glance, and its copy on the server is deleted by the next sync. A forgotten PIN cannot be got around; those notes are lost - Every floating button is a filled rounded square, the same as in the other apps - The scrollbar shows the right place when one item is taller than the screen
## Fixed
- Signing in again to the same account, by email or by name, keeps the notes on the phone and the task lists - Settings shows the server the same way for every account, with its port when it is not the usual one

entry.title: Songbook 0.1.14

# Songbook 0.1.14
- Where Home (the launcher) is signed in to a Nextcloud, the Nextcloud screen has a new row: "Use the phone's Nextcloud account". Songbook then uses Home's account instead of its own sign-in, takes a new app password from Home, and signs out when Home does, with your songs and setlists left on the phone. entry.title: Datebook 0.1.73

The account then shows "<name> on <server>, from Home." with "Stop using it" - Using Home's account replaces only your sign-ins on that same server; accounts on other servers stay. You are asked a second time only when something will be removed - A new password in Home reaches Datebook on its own. If Home signs out or is removed, Datebook stops syncing and drops its copy of the password; your calendars stay on the phone - Without Home, signing in works as before - The scrollbar shows where you are on a page that holds a row taller than the screen

entry.title: Connections 0.2.41
entry.content:
# Connections 0.2.41
- Where Home is signed in to a Nextcloud, Settings, Contacts server has one row, "Use the phone's Nextcloud account": it syncs your contacts with that account, with no password to type - The app takes the account only from the real Home, and keeps only which account it chose; the password stays Home's and is read from Home again before each sync - When Home signs out, or signs in to another account, this app stops syncing with it too and says so; your contacts stay on the phone - Stop using it takes that account and its people off the phone; the server keeps them - The account it makes on the phone is named user@host, as one you sign in to yourself, with the port when it is not the usual one - A sign-in you made yourself for the same account is taken over, after its waiting changes are sent; one whose changes cannot be sent stays, and the page says so
## Fixed
- A scrollbar beside a row taller than the screen shows where you are in it - A second pull while it is syncing asks nothing more

entry.title: Feeds 0.6.20
entry.content:
# Feeds 0.6.20
- Sync with a feed server has a Use the phone's Nextcloud account row when Home is signed in to Nextcloud: Feeds then syncs with that Nextcloud's News app, with no password typed here - Home keeps the password; Feeds asks Home for it before each sync and when it opens, and holds it in memory only - When Home signs out of Nextcloud, Feeds stops syncing and says so, with no error; feeds and articles stay on the phone. When Home signs in to another account, Feeds forgets the old one until the row is pressed again - Stop using it goes back to the app's own sign-in - A feed server you sync with sees the app as "Feeds" in its log; feeds and sites still see the old name - With Feeds closed, the play button on headphones, in a car or in a navigation app carries on with the podcast episode heard last, where it stopped; one heard to the end is not started again
## Fixed
- Pressing Sync while a sync with the feed server runs does nothing, instead of starting the sync over - In a list where one item is taller than the screen, the scrollbar shows where you are in it

entry.title: Dream Log 0.1.38

# Dream Log 0.1.38
- Settings > Nextcloud has "Use the phone's Nextcloud account": if Home, the launcher, is signed in to Nextcloud, Dream Log can use that account, with no sign-in of its own - Only the real Home is asked, checked by its name and signature; Dream Log keeps nothing of the password, asks Home for it again when it needs it, and holds it in memory only - When Home signs out or is removed, Dream Log is signed out too and stops sending; your dreams stay on the phone, and copies already in Nextcloud stay - "Stop using it" lets Home's account go here and leaves Home signed in, so you can sign in here instead - The server is shown the same way for both kinds of account: no https://, no slash at the end
## Fixed
- Dreams go to the right Nextcloud folder when the user's login name is not their user id, as with an email address - A dream longer than the screen has a scrollbar that shows where you are in it

entry.title: Messaging 1.35.44
entry.content:
# Messaging 1.35.44
- A passphrase lock, off unless you turn it on (Settings, Display, Passphrase lock). While locked, Signal messages and calls wait until you unlock, Desktop Sync stops, and a text shows only that something arrived; it is brought into the app when you unlock. It locks when the screen turns off, a set time after you leave the app, or when you choose Lock now, never during a call. If the passphrase is forgotten, the only way back is to clear the app's data and link Signal again - When the lock closes, the memory the app used is overwritten, so nothing read can be recovered from it (can be turned off) - Backups are encrypted with a 30-digit backup code, made once and shown for writing down; no backup is made without one. To restore on another phone, enter that phone's code first. Older backups still restore - Automatic backups, daily or weekly, keeping the newest 1 to 10 - The backup location row names the folder in use - An optional SOCKS proxy for Signal (Settings, Signal), for example Orbot for Tor. Signal calls are off while it is on, because they cannot go through it - In a conversation with disappearing messages, call lines disappear with the messages - Signal's encryption library is updated to 0.108.0, as Signal Android uses it
## Fixed
- An edit of a view-once message no longer makes its picture last - Settings no longer stops responding when many Signal updates arrive at once

# Tuner 0.1.53

entry.title: Shelf 0.1.40
entry.content:
# Shelf 0.1.40
- The bar with Scan and Shelf order is the same height as the other apps' top bars - Spreadsheet export keeps every text cell from running as a formula, and a book known only by its LCCN survives the round trip - A QR sign-in is checked with the server before it is kept - Books found without the Library of Congress are looked up there again quietly, two a minute and never ahead of a fresh scan; with no connection, the asking waits for one to come back - The tabs always fit across the screen - Listen asks only the real Audio Reader, before a title goes out or a book is opened - Dark mode and the file picker trust only the real Home and Cabinet apps; once Home is removed, the app's own dark setting applies again, and it keeps its last setting while Home is briefly unavailable, as during its update
## Fixed
- Sync compares files from a compressing web server as the same file - An unreadable catalog is kept aside, and a failed write no longer closes the app - Nothing is saved, synced or imported until the library has loaded, and a book added meanwhile is kept - Import matches a row known by its LCCN alone, so books still waiting for a lookup no longer hide it as already here - A Dewey number with a stray mark is saved clean and no longer crashes Sections - A lookup only the unreachable catalogs might know is a miss, not tried every minute - Genre fill with a catalog out of reach waits for the next start instead of ending for good - A tap on the scrollbar lands on the right row after the screen changes

entry.title: Atlas 0.1.15
entry.content:
# Atlas 0.1.15
- Follow trail: Walk to here follows a trail from where you meet it to the spot marked on it, kept across restarts; away from the trail, Walk to the trail plans a walking route to its nearest point - Walk to here has its own icon: a walking figure with a flag ahead - Dark mode reaches the wait dialogs for moving maps and sharing or importing bookmarks; the streamed map and the OpenStreetMap profile picture keep their colors - Own-server dialogs say that a plain http:// address is taken for a server at home, and is sent unencrypted - A contact's address tapped into the search, or used for directions from the place screen, is not kept in the search history - A bug report carries the phone's system information as text in the mail rather than the app's log, and log archives left by earlier reports are deleted - Place types use US English (Highway, not Motorway); British and New Zealand English keep Motorway - Bookmark notes load nothing from the network, so a picture in an imported note does not tell its server the place was opened - Dark mode takes Home's switch only from the real Home app, and the app's own setting applies again once Home is removed; it keeps its last setting while Home is briefly unavailable, as during its update
## Fixed
- Walk to here starts from a fresh, close position, stops on the pass of the trail that was marked, and finds the marked spot on a trail made of several lines; deleting the followed track ends following - An online address lookup tries Photon when the Census geocoder cannot be reached - Fastest for one trip no longer turns off avoid-motorways set in Settings - On a phone that turns sideways, the navigation and downloader panels no longer close the app - Another app can no longer plan a route through the map's own extras, or close the app with a bookmark or track that is gone - Search asks Contacts off the main thread as you type - A tap on the scrollbar lands on the right row after the screen changes

entry.title: Birding 1.7.48
entry.content:
# Birding 1.7.48
- A place gone stale or unknown stops weighing the answers, and a detection is no longer stamped with a stale place, even with the screen left in front - Listening lets go of the microphone on stop - The species list keeps its search across a return - The app keeps its English name in every language, so it is never taken for the phone's own app - Dark mode and the file picker trust only the real Home and Cabinet apps; once Home is removed, the app's own dark setting applies again, and it keeps its last setting while Home is briefly unavailable, as during its update
## Fixed
- A newer run of the same bird no longer crashes the app with a duplicate row - Restore keeps the old log until the new one has been read, and detections after a restore land in the restored log - A restore on a full phone says the phone is too full, not that the backup is damaged - A backup naming a bird the app has no name for is refused, and the log leaves such a line off rather than failing on it - Removing a row from the condensed Heard log no longer takes another day's readings with it - A microphone that will not open says Not listening with a notice why, and a press to listen tries again - A recording is written whole or not at all, and recordings kept for the session are no longer cleared by a change of font size, language or dark mode - Species names with a comma are quoted in the spreadsheet - A tap on the scrollbar lands on the right row after the screen changes

entry.title: Chess+ 1.3.30-chessplus
entry.content:
# Chess+ 1.3.30
- When the engine fails while choosing a move it is started again; if it still cannot play, the game is kept, not resigned and deleted - A saved game that cannot be read is no longer deleted silently: a message offers Keep or Discard, and a new game over it asks first - Two players: Undo with a move placed but not confirmed takes back only that move - New game saves the chosen difficulty and move hints before the game starts - Statistics: Clear all asks with a second tap on the button instead of a dialog - The app keeps its English name in every language, so it is never taken for the phone's own app - Dark mode takes Home's switch only from the real Home app, and the app's own setting applies again once Home is removed; it keeps its last setting while Home is briefly unavailable, as during its update
## Fixed
- An engine that stops answering is ended after two seconds and started again on the next move, and a restarted engine is no longer disturbed by the old one - Leaving the no-engine message goes back to the menu without bringing the message back - A damaged copy of the engine's net is made again instead of staying missing - A computer move canceled before its search began no longer waits forever - A tap on the scrollbar lands on the right row after the screen changes

entry.title: Topo 0.2.22
entry.content:
# Topo 0.2.22
- A Geocaches map layer, off until added under Layers: open a geocache GPX file or Pocket Query zip from the map menu or another app, and, with signal, see the Opencaching sites' caches for the map on the screen. Each cache shows its kind, a tick once found and a cross after a did-not-find; its sheet has the hint, the description, Navigate, Found it, Not found and a note. Field notes export for Geocaching.com or Opencaching. A saved area keeps its caches too - Save this area tries a failed tile again after a pause; an area that could not be fetched in full says how many map and elevation tiles are missing and offers to fetch just those - Save this area still fetches the map tiles when the elevation server is out of reach, and an elevation tile the server does not have is not counted as missing - Save this area says when the fruit and nut trees or the streets could not be kept with it - Opening a GPX file of waypoints asks before adding them as beacons and turns down a file of thousands - Backup says that saved areas are not in it and are saved again on a new phone - Settings has an Open DuraSpeed row on a phone that has DuraSpeed - My region packs only keeps the Forage and Streets layers off the network too - Dark mode takes Home's switch only from the real Home app, and the app's own setting applies again once Home is removed; it keeps its last setting while Home is briefly unavailable, as during its update
## Fixed
- The bottom bar says Navigate in full, rather than a cut-off Navigat... - The Location and Elevation home-screen widgets draw again rather than closing the app on each update - Backups restore again when saved areas or the Forage and Streets layers hold many files: tiles are left out and fetched again on use - Zoomed-out and edge map tiles a saved area kept are drawn with no signal too - Deleting a saved area finishes removing its tiles even if the page is left part way, and tiles left by a save that failed or was closed are removed - Importing or removing an elevation model touches that model only; a zip that is not an elevation model leaves the loaded one as it was, and a model imported before this version is removed by Remove and replaced by a new import - A region pack named like the viewed terrain, the imported model or a saved area's elevation no longer replaces it - A region pack download left part way is not reported as a failure, and leaves no partial file - A tap on the scrollbar lands on the right row after the screen changes

entry.title: Detour 0.1.31
entry.content:
# Detour 0.1.31
- The walk's destination survives the app being stopped in the background - Back from Settings returns to the walk - Settings turns its pages like the app's other lists - The GPS and the compass are let go while the screen is away and start again on the way back - Arrived is said only from a live position sure to within 50 meters - Dark mode takes Home's switch only from the real Home app, and the app's own setting applies again once Home is removed; it keeps its last setting while Home is briefly unavailable, as during its update
## Fixed
- A newer GPS fix is always taken, even a little less sure than the last, and a clock set back during a walk no longer freezes the position - A permission dialog closed with Back is not taken as refused for good, Ask every time still asks again, and a refusal Android stopped asking about is recognized in later runs - A tap on the scrollbar lands on the right row after the screen changes

entry.title: Audio Reader 1.3.69
entry.content:
# Audio Reader 1.3.69
- A book whose first file is renamed, or gains a file in front, keeps its place, bookmarks and chapter marks - Listening on after the screen is gone keeps its place - A file another app opens comes in paused, so playback starts only when you press play - Server sync: a downloaded book whose file changes on the server goes back to Download, which fetches the new file instead of the player stopping at it; while it waits, the book stays in Downloaded and can still be removed - Only the app, the system and the controllers it vouches for (notification, Bluetooth, lock screen) can see or steer what is playing, and Open with takes only a file or a document - On Android 13 and later, notifications are asked for once, the first time a book is kept - Dark mode and the file picker trust only the real Home and Cabinet apps; once Home is removed, the app's own dark setting applies again, and it keeps its last setting while Home is briefly unavailable, as during its update
## Fixed
- A folder that fails to list part way keeps its books, places and bookmarks - A file gone from a book's folder leaves its chapter list, so the player no longer stops at it; a file the server no longer has leaves it too, unless its audio is on the phone, so the book can be downloaded again - Restoring places moves the book in the strip and in the player, so Play does not carry on from the old place - Opening the book already in the player carries on from where it is, instead of going a few seconds back - Opening a book in a player stopped from a headset plays instead of sitting still - An odd Audiobookshelf answer says "not Audiobookshelf" instead of crashing the app; a pasted key loses the line break it brought, and a key that cannot be used is said in words instead of crashing - Lengths and tags are read on Android 9 too - A tap on the scrollbar lands on the right row after the screen changes

entry.title: Bitcoin 0.1.18
entry.content:

## Fixed
- A failed price fetch waits a minute before trying again, and a rate more than an hour old is not used - A lock-screen price for the currency just changed from is dropped - A payment link opens Send once, not again when the app is recreated or reopened from Recents - The backup Electrum server stays chosen when two connections both find the first not answering - The fingerprint prompt comes up without a pause - An answered fingerprint notice no longer comes back after another change to the wallet, such as its passphrase setting - The connected notification of a hardware wallet that is not remembered opens it again - Hardware wallet replies are logged only in debug builds - A tap on the scrollbar lands on the right row after the screen changes
